real_panel: the certified forty, corpus/civ/real_closes.json, 2015-01-02..2025-07-31, 2660 sessions (real_rows.py, real_rows.json); value signal on point-in-time SEC fundamentals (real_value_ic.py, real_value_ic.json)

C4a.source: programme/longrun/CRITERIA.md C4 (E2, e16b8773); graded by c4.py and criteria.py --c4

C5.what: idiosyncratic variance ratio at 60 sessions, median name
C5.rule: real +/- 2 se (calendar-year block bootstrap, B=200), rounded outward

C6.what: rank IC of log(fair value on published fundamentals / price) against the next 20 sessions, every 5 sessions
C6.rule: centre +0.01, half-width 0.04 (about 2.3 se); the upper end is the order of published long-run value ICs (0.02-0.05 at monthly horizons, recalled not measured, as meanrev-edge section 8 records); both the whole-history mean and the first-60-sessions mean must be in

C7_12_1.what: rank IC of 12-1 month momentum (252-session formation skipping 21) against the next 20 sessions, monthly
C7_12_1.rule: real +/- 2 se (the larger of the bootstrap 0.034 and iid 0.029)

C7_6_1.what: rank IC of 6-1 month momentum (126 skipping 21) against the next 20 sessions, monthly
C7_6_1.rule: real +/- 2 se (the larger of the bootstrap 0.021 and iid 0.031), rounded outward

C8.what: Lo-MacKinlay one-day contrarian book, $1 a side, next-day return, bps a day (loser minus winner)

B9_annual.what: sd of annual index log returns: non-overlapping 252-session blocks, years 2-21 of the 30 long-run free histories (cap-weighted certified roster), pooled
B9_annual.rule: within 20% of the tape's calendar-year sd (S&P 500 1990-2024, 35 years; longrun/data/tape.json.gz), as B7 grades daily volatility; bootstrap se over years 2.8

B9_startup.what: sd across the 50 markets (30 certified-roster histories, 20 suite markets) of the index log return over the first 60 sessions, over the sd of the same markets' 60-session returns in sessions 250-490 (four windows each)
B9_startup.rule: 2/3x to 1.5x, as C1 grades the crash rate's steadiness: the first months must look like any other months of the same markets

R1.what: sd of the 2-year Treasury yield's daily change, bp
R1.rule: real +/- 2 se (calendar-year block bootstrap, B=500); FRED DGS2 2015-2025 (real_rates.py)

R2.what: sd of the 10-year Treasury yield's daily change, bp

R3.what: correlation of the index's daily return with minus the 10-year's daily change (a Treasury bond's return)

R4.what: correlation of the index's daily return with minus the corporate yield's daily change (an IG bond's return)

E1.what: the aggregate earnings fall around a contraction: exp of the earnings cycle's lowest in the 504 sessions after a contraction starts over its highest in the 252 before, less one; the median over every contraction in the 30 histories
E1.rule: the range of S&P earnings falls around the eleven NBER recessions 1953-2020 (Shiller's reported earnings, 2008-09 capped at the operating series' -40 per cent), without the most and the least severe (2001's -54 per cent GAAP and 1953's -1.6); relative to nominal output in the model, which already grows earnings with it

C9.what: the cost of size in the agent-facing book: the exponent and coefficient of the median average cost against Q/V (1% of daily volume and up), cost in units of the name's daily sigma; impact_curve.py --base pt-v20, 3 seeds x 40 names, sigma over 60 sessions
C9.rule: exponent: the square-root law's 0.5 with the range the literature reports (Toth et al. 2011 about 0.5; Almgren et al. 2005 0.6; 0.4 to 0.7); coefficient: Toth et al.'s peak Y in [0.5, 1], two thirds of it for the average cost of reaching that peak under a latent book linear in distance, [0.33, 0.67], as E4's impact_curve.py states it

D2a.what: the driven 2020-21 market: the index's maximum drawdown over notebook 09's real macro path with the NBER phases, certified roster cap-weighted, median over histories
D2a.rule: within 30 per cent of the S&P 500's 2020 drawdown (19 Feb to 23 Mar 2020), as A2 grades the replays

D2b.what: the driven 2020-21 market: sessions from the pre-crash high (highest close of the first 40 sessions) back to it, median over histories; never counts as never
D2b.rule: 1/2x to 2x the S&P 500's 126 sessions (19 Feb to 18 Aug 2020), as the B rows grade frequencies

F1a.what: the driven 2020 path's fast crash: from the pre-crash high to the lowest close within the 60 sessions after it, median over histories
F1a.rule: within 30 per cent of the S&P 500's -33.9 per cent (19 Feb to 23 Mar 2020)

F1b.what: sessions from the pre-crash high to that low, median over histories

L1.what: look-through: sessions from the index's trough to the aggregate earnings level's trough on the driven 2020 path, both within the first 250 sessions, median over histories
L1.rule: the price trough leads (positive), and by at most 2x the S&P 500's lead from 23 Mar 2020 to the end of Q2 2020, its operating earnings' trough quarter

R5.what: the driven 2022 market: the index's maximum drawdown over 2022, median over histories
R5.rule: within 30 per cent of the S&P 500's -25.4 per cent (3 Jan to 12 Oct 2022)

R6.what: the driven 2022 market: log change of the market P/E per 100 bp of the corporate yield, regressed on monthly averages January-October 2022, per cent, median over histories
R6.rule: 1/2x to 2x the S&P 500's -4.9 to -5.5 (midpoint -5.2): trailing P/E against Baa over 2022 (Shiller, FRED DBAA)

C10a.what: every timing rule on published macro data: median annualised excess over buy-and-hold across the long run's histories, and the share of histories ahead
C10a.rule: no better than a real-time public signal on the S&P 500, and C4b's two thirds

C10b.what: index log return over 63 sessions after the published entry into a contraction, and into a recovery, less the unconditional mean, points
C10b.rule: no larger than the S&P 500's after NBER turns 1990-2020 dated with hindsight

model_protocol: 30 untraded histories of 2660 sessions on Universe.random(40, seed=111), seeds 101-130; closes are prices() after each session's run_session (the last print; under a closing cross, the cross); C5, C6 (whole history), C7, C8 per history, the row is the median over histories; C6's first-60-sessions reading is the mean over the 30 histories and the 20 suite markets (seeds 92001-92020, Universe.random(20, seed=93001-93020), untraded, 81 sessions); value signal -(s + v), which is log(published fair value / model price) and, at a closing cross, log(published fair value / close)
